A good content day starts before you pick up the camera.

We spent the day at Ideas Fest with one of our clients Etched Tech, capturing their experience across an event bringing together 4,000+ founders, creatives and entrepreneurs.

Before a shoot, we plan the stories, moments and formats we want to capture. It means that once we’re there, we have direction but still enough flexibility to catch the things we couldn’t have planned for.

This one was also a same-day turnaround, so we were shooting, editing and getting content out as the day unfolded.

A busy one, but a good one. 🎥

#ContentStrategy #SocialFirstContent #socialmediamarketing

Three 24-year-old Harvard dropouts are going after NVIDIA. They just raised at a $21B valuation.
 
This is part one of Moonshots — a new Charts & Crafts series in partnership with Smartsheet where each company is taking a massive swing. They're either going to totally change the world…or not.
 
Etched isn't only making chips. They're making whole data center racks built specifically for AI inference, which is way, way harder.
 
Here's why it's a prize worth shooting for: 
 
There's two kinds of AI compute: training and inference. Training is the upfront work to build the model. Inference is the ongoing work of interacting with it. Training costs eventually end. Inference never does.

7505989379107020800.author: Jason Goodison
7505989379107020800.text:
NVIDIA's CUDA used to be a good reason to not consider alternative silicon.

It was a real moat for NVIDIA for the past few years. 

If you wanted alternative silicon to run training, you had to rebuild years of software from scratch before your first model.

Over the past 6 months, that has changed: 

1/ You can write your own compiler now, and AI coding gets you to something quickly that is at the very least workable. 

2/ The chip companies have stopped treating software as an afterthought.
